messages.author: 762340260270eefa
messages.subject: DataTables advanced options (functions)
parts:
Shiny 0.8 has been great so far, especially thanks to the added direct support of DataTables.  I have successfully played around with most of the options available to DataTables, but I am having trouble with fnCreatedCell.  I found this discussion on the rCharts github, but the advice there does not seem to work, I still get the same error:

  1. Uncaught TypeError: Object #! function(nTd, sData, oData, iRow, iCol){ if (sData > 350){ $(nTd).css('color', 'red'); } } !# has no method 'call' jquery.dataTables.min.js:33

Has anyone had any success using functions within DataTables options?

Thanks,
Scott

PS - The example I am trying is trivial, just making a renderDataTable with the mtcars data:

output$datatable <- renderDataTable({ mtcars }, options = list(aoColumnDefs = list(list(
    aTargets = list(2),
    fnCreatedCell = "#! function(nTd, sData, oData, iRow, iCol){
      if (sData > 350){
         $(nTd).css('color', 'red');
      }
    } !#")))
  );

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: DataTables advanced options (functions)
parts:
At the moment, I guess we are not yet able to go that far to pass a
JavaScript function to DataTables, since it seems there is no way for
the RJSONIO package to do the conversion (I might be wrong). I'm
curious where the syntax "#! function !#" was from -- is that a
convention in RJSONIO or a custom invention of rCharts?

We will definitely consider more about advanced customization in
future versions. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

Hi,

I take profit of this thread title as I got a problem with some DT advanced options.

I'm trying to customize the reaction of my DT, and I want to make my search field case insensitive.
DataTables have an option for this :
bCaseInsensitive

Here's what I do :
output$mytable <- renderDataTable({
        someTable()
    }, options= list(bSortClasses = TRUE,
                     oSearch = list(
                         sSearch= "",
                         bCaseInsensitive=TRUE
                         )
                     )
    )

My problem is that sSearch works (initial search text), but bCaseInsensitive (be it false or true) never works : when I look for a field with uppercases, it doesn't find it.

Any idea ?

Thanks,

Robin

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: DataTables advanced options (functions)
parts:
Yes. #! function !# was a hack in rCharts. It is used to pass literal javascript objects to the payload, and this includes functions and javascript objects (that you want to send unquoted).

I searched extensively for a solution that is standard, but was unable to figure it out, and the #! ... !# is a unique enough pattern that it is not going to interfere with regular text.

If there is a standard way of doing this, I would like to know.

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: DataTables advanced options (functions)
parts:
At the moment, the search text is treated as regular expressions in R
by default, and there are a couple of features that are not
implemented yet on shiny's side. For your case, a probably awkward
solution is to use regular expressions like [Aa]pple to search for
"apple" or "Apple". Unfortunately, the DataTables library does not
seem to pass the bCaseInsensitive option to the server side
(http://datatables.net/usage/server-side), so we cannot make use of it
(note that renderDataTable() uses server-side processing, i.e. it is R
that processes the data).

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: DataTables advanced options (functions)
parts:
That sounds like a smart work around, but RJSONIO does not seem to
support literal symbols, e.g. RJSONIO::toJSON('foo') gives a quoted
string ["foo"], and there is no way to generate foo. I think that is
why Ramnath used a special character string "#! foo !#" to "protect"
the symbol, and restore it later. There is only a limited number of
data types supported in the conversion between R and JSON data.

Regards,
Yihui

Unfortunately, the answer is still no. I cannot do much on shiny's
side unless DataTables passes the info search[caseInsensitive] over to
the server-side processing: https://datatables.net/manual/server-side

file a feature request to the DataTables library:
https://datatables.net/forums/ or
https://github.com/DataTables/DataTables/issues

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: DataTables advanced options (functions)
parts:
I have implemented case-insensitive searching:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/579 Hopefully this will appear
in the next version of shiny (0.10.2). Please note that the parameter
name bCaseInsensitve no longer works; now it should be

renderDataTable(..., options = list(search = list(caseInsensitive = TRUE)))

but you do not really need to set it, since it is the default value.
You only need it when you want to go back to the case-sensitive
matching:

renderDataTable(..., options = list(search = list(caseInsensitive = FALSE)))

Regards,
Yihui
